clue.text: Bereaved woman welcoming new opportunity for action

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a woman whose husband has died
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A grieving widow finds a fresh chance to do something with her life.
explanation.walkthrough: N sits inside WIDOW to make WINDOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A window is a limited period of opportunity, as in a window to act before a deadline.

clue.text: Muslim ambassador embracing community leader

indicators.note: the words hold the solution within their arms, spanning the gap between them

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A Muslim diplomat hugs the head of a local community.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is spelt out across muslIM AMbassador; 'Muslim' looks like part of the definition but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque and is the religious head of a Muslim congregation.

clue.text: Bestow money on extremely loyal old sculptor

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: to donate is to give money away
the first and last letters of loyal
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A patron rewards a faithful, aged artist with a gift of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old sculptor' looks like one phrase, but 'old' supplies a letter and only 'sculptor' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatello was a Florentine Renaissance sculptor of the fifteenth century, famous for his bronze David.

clue.text: Everything put in foolish place to store money

indicators.note: putting one thing in another means placing it inside

blocks.note: wet is British slang for feeble or silly
all means everything

explanation.surface: Putting all your savings somewhere silly is unwise.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a wet person is feeble or foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallet is a small folding case carried in a pocket for keeping banknotes and cards.

clue.text: Find hybrid pig in new Canadian city

indicators.note: a hybrid is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A crossbred pig turns up in a newly built town in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnipeg is the capital of the province of Manitoba in central Canada.

clue.text: Having the most sincere intentions (expressed by having the most perfect legal document)

annotation.answer: WITH THE BEST WILL IN THE WORLD

definitions.text: having the most perfect legal document

blocks.note: first meaning: an idiom for trying as hard as you possibly can

blocks.clueFragment: having the most perfect legal document
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: owning the finest testament anywhere

explanation.surface: A wry aside that good intentions are best shown by a watertight will.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the idiom word by word: a will is the legal document that leaves your estate, and the best one in the world is the most perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, usually followed by a 'but', means however hard one tries or however good one's motives.

clue.text: Turned up at home to score drug twice at beginning of night, just before half eleven

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning something up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: at home is IN, here turned upwards
to net is to score a goal
E is ecstasy, taken twice
N is the abbreviation for night

explanation.surface: A clubber comes home, scores drugs and is out before half past ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half eleven' sounds like 10.30, but it means half of 11-across, TWENTY TWENTY: the number that comes just before twenty is NINETEEN. EE is placed at the start of N.
explanation.definitionFit: Half of the 11-across answer is twenty, and nineteen is the number immediately preceding twenty.

clue.text: See 5
Shield with coat of arms features queen's penultimate hairdo in badly-chosen surroundings

indicators.note: something done badly is done wrongly, so the letters come out in the wrong order
surroundings enclose whatever sits in the middle of them
penultimate means last but one, so only that letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: the next-to-last letter of queen
taken as written, then mixed with the letter from queen
a haircut, or cut, is a hairdo

explanation.surface: A heraldic shield shows the queen with an unfortunate haircut amid a poorly picked backdrop.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen's letter joins the scrambled CHOSEN, and the hairdo sits in the middle of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An escutcheon is the shield-shaped surface on which a coat of arms is displayed in heraldry.

clue.text: Glove stolen by thieving Aunt Letitia

indicators.note: something stolen by the following words is held inside them

blocks.note: spans the end of thieving, all of Aunt, and the start of Letitia

explanation.surface: A light-fingered aunt has pinched someone's glove.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through thievinG AUNT LETitia.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauntlet is a strong glove with a long cuff, originally part of armour.

clue.text: Bill has no time to get something to put in drink

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
ice cubes go in a drink

explanation.surface: Bill is in a hurry to fetch a cube for his glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is the definition, a printed poster.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a posted announcement or placard, which is also called a notice.

clue.text: Normal vision needed for this form of cricket?

blocks.note: first meaning: the standard score on an eye test
second meaning: the short game of twenty overs a side

explanation.surface: A batter needs good eyesight to play a certain type of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Twenty20 is a fast cricket format in which each team bats for twenty overs.
explanation.definitionFit: Opticians describe average eyesight as 20/20, and the abbreviated cricket match is named after its overs per innings.

clue.text: Labourer's bird eating battered cod

indicators.note: battered means beaten out of shape, so the letters are knocked about
eating means taking something inside

blocks.note: a harrier is a bird of prey
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A building worker's pet bird tucks into fish in batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battered cod' reads as a chip-shop dish, but battered is the signal; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hod carrier is a building site labourer who carries bricks or mortar in a hod.

clue.text: Container for blackbird

blocks.note: read the word as black then bird: B is the opening letter, the standard abbreviation for black
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: Somewhere to keep a blackbird, like a cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blackbird' must be split into two words, black then bird; B for black is standard in pencil grading.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl is a round open dish used to hold food or liquid.

clue.text: Setter taking position said to make sense

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the words are judged by how they sound

blocks.note: the setter refers to themselves as I
a site is a position

explanation.surface: A setter takes a view on something to help it make sense.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is I, and the two spoken words are spelt as different words with the same sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of vision, one of the five senses.

clue.text: Illinois soldier in nearby pub is not making sense

indicators.note: a soldier in somewhere is placed inside it

blocks.note: IL is the postal abbreviation for Illinois
a local is the pub near your home
GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier from Illinois drinking at the local is talking nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is British slang for the neighbourhood pub; 'is' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illogical lacks sound reasoning and so does not make sense.

clue.text: Competitor not expected to win is grounded, anyway

indicators.note: any way means in whatever arrangement, so the letters may be put in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The outsider is grounded and out of contention whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' reads as a shrug at the end of the sentence, but split as 'any way' it signals the letters can be arranged freely.
explanation.definitionFit: An underdog is the side thought likely to lose a contest.

clue.text: Crusoe arranged to get hold of new source of gunpowder to cadge

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order
the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
N is the abbreviation for new
the first letter of gunpowder

explanation.surface: Robinson Crusoe, stranded, sets out to beg for some gunpowder.
explanation.walkthrough: N and G join the letters of CRUSOE before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrounge is to get something by begging or wheedling rather than paying, which is what cadge means.

clue.text: Appear in toilet at end of break

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: loo is British slang for a toilet
the last letter of break

explanation.surface: Someone shows up in the lavatory once the interval is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To look a certain way is to appear or seem that way, as in 'she looks tired'.

clue.text: Choose Rob in audition for The Garden Party?

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the words are taken by their sound

blocks.note: to pick is to choose
to nick is British slang for to steal

explanation.surface: A director picks an actor called Rob to play in a staging of Katherine Mansfield's story The Garden Party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Garden Party is a Katherine Mansfield story, but the question mark tells us to read it loosely as a party held in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnic is an outdoor meal eaten by a group, so it is a sort of party out of doors.

clue.text: Men twirl rags furiously in test of strength

indicators.note: done furiously, the letters are thrown about wildly

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Men whirl cloths around wildly as part of a strongman contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Arm wrestling is a contest in which two people try to force each other's forearm down onto a table.

clue.text: See 5
Joint in pipework needed

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A plumber says a connecting joint is required in the pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' sounds like plumbing, but here it is the body's joint, spelt across pipeworK NEEded.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the joint between the thigh and the lower leg.

clue.text: Hunter changed mind about returning gold

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters move into a new order
returning means going back the way it came, so it reads backwards
about means around, so one part goes round the other

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
or is heraldic gold, here read backwards

explanation.surface: A hunter has a change of heart about bringing back the gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Or is the heraldic word for gold, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimrod is the mighty hunter of Genesis, and his name is used for any keen hunter.

clue.text: Place to drink to Flintoff's sixth hundred is spotless

indicators.note: sixth points to the letter in that position of the name

blocks.note: an inn is a pub
the sixth letter of Flintoff
cent means a hundred, as in century

explanation.surface: A toast in the pub to cricketer Andrew Flintoff's century is without blemish.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Flintoff is a former England cricketer, so 'hundred' looks like a century scored by him; the 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocent means free from guilt or sin, so morally spotless.

clue.text: Urge one lass to be extravagant with money

blocks.note: to prod is to urge on
I is the Roman numeral one
gal is a girl or lass

explanation.surface: A parent urges a girl to spend freely.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigal means wastefully lavish, as in the prodigal son who squandered his inheritance.

clue.text: Less friendly Chinese leader not getting any younger

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

blocks.note: the first letter of Chinese
someone not getting younger is growing older

explanation.surface: An ageing Chinese ruler grows frostier with the years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinese leader' suggests a head of state, but it only gives the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold describes an unfriendly manner, so colder means more distant and less warm.
